neighbours.label: the preposition or possessive that introduces whose benefit or what purpose something is used or exploited for ('exploit it for', 'use them to their advantage', 'abuse power for private gain'; Spanish 'para'), as against the same prepositions after verbs of waiting, buying or working
fire: Critics say the minister exploited the tragedy for political points.
Smart investors use market panics to their advantage.
She was fired for misusing company funds for her own holidays.
The rebels turned the mountains to their advantage.
Officials who abuse power for private gain must be punished.
Farmers can harness the wind for cheap electricity.
Las empresas utilizan los datos para mejorar sus productos.
He leveraged his fame for charitable causes.
quiet: Critics say the minister waited for the tragedy report.
Smart investors sell stocks to their brokers.
She was fired for arriving late for her shifts.
The rebels walked to their camp in the mountains.
Officials who work for the city must be punctual.
Farmers can wait for the wind to drop.
Las empresas venden los datos a otras empresas.
He looked for his keys in the car.

predictions: fire 0.4-0.65 on for/to/their/para after use/exploit/abuse verbs; temporal or recipient 'for/to' below 0.05
